name: ai-openai
summary: OpenAI provider for the jPulse AI agent
description: Streams OpenAI Responses API completions into the ai-core turn loop. The API key is type: "password": bulk reads return ********, completions use PluginModel.getSecret, and Verify pings /v1/models without returning the key.
author: jPulse Team <team@jpulse.net>

schema.content: OpenAI API key for the site AI agent. Verify uses the value in the field (you do not need to Save first). The key never comes back in the Verify response.

schema.label: API key
schema.help: Masked in GET config. Reveal on this form is audited. Completions read the stored value on the server.

schema.label: Verify API key
schema.help: Calls GET /v1/models with the key in this field. Unsaved is fine. The button never receives the stored-only value.

schema.label: Default model
schema.help: Used when Site Configuration → AI does not pick a model.

schema.label: API endpoint
schema.help: No trailing path. Completions POST {endpoint}/v1/responses; Verify GET {endpoint}/v1/models.

schema.label: Request timeout (ms)
schema.help: Abort one HTTP request after this many milliseconds.

schema.content:
Leave empty to use the built-in prices (USD per million tokens, short-context Standard, verified 2026-09-26 from OpenAI). Cache write is the 1.25× input rate. An unknown model stores cost null — it must not cost $0.

To override, paste a JSON object. Keys are model ids. Each value needs four numbers — input, output, cacheWrite, cacheRead — in $/MTok.

Example:

{ "gpt-6-sol": { "input": 2, "output": 10, "cacheWrite": 2.5, "cacheRead": 0.2 } }

You may list several models. Invalid JSON is ignored and the built-in table stays in effect.

schema.label: Price table override
schema.help: Empty = built-in table. JSON object of model-id → { input, output, cacheWrite, cacheRead } in USD per million tokens.
